# Overview

DNS is a system which binds hostnames or URIs to IPs. Ansible will set up most of this automatically but there are some things that need to be configured before deploying.

## Configuration

By default, every environment/branch is deployed with DNS.

You can change this by setting `dns.deploy` to `false` in `deployment_config.yml`.

```yaml
dns:
  deploy: true
  dnssec: true # whether to use dnssec or not
```

## Automatically Generated DNS names

DNS names are automatically generated for every system.

In general, when deploying a system directly through `deployment_config.yml`, then the generated name will be in the format `<machine_name>.<system_name>.lab`

In a lab configuration, the generated name becomes a bit more complex. The generated name will be of the form `<system_name>_<machine_name>.<lab_name>.lab`

## Supported Records

`A` records - Handles IPv4 connections. A name is automatically generated for each machine in the environment. Remember that only the jumpbox is able to access all machines.

`AAAA` records - Handles IPv6 connections. A name is automatically generated for each machine in the environment. Remember that only the jumpbox is able to access all machines.

`MX` records - Handles Mail server records. Mail services are generated for each environment, that is, each environment will be granted an autogenerated email, in the form of `<env>.mail`, such as `example.mail`.

`SRV` records - Holds details for port bindings. This allows you to call certain domain names and get the details for resolving to that host name.
For instance, if I wanted to get the details for a website hosted at `http://worker_1.example.lab:3000`, and I had an SRV record which specified the protocol, service, and host that would point to said website, I would be able to extract the original hostname, which is `worker_1.example.lab`, and the port, which is `3000`. I can then use these details to build my url and connect to the webserver over http. 
However this is all in theory, and many services do not inherently resolve SRV records, so this is more for record keeping at present.

## Specifying Custom URIs

Ports in any `values.yml` will get translated into custom URIs. Ones with a port specified become SRV records, and ones without become A/AAAA records.

```yml
ports:
  dashboard:
    port: 5000
    service: http
    protocol: tcp
    machine: server
  health:
    machine: server
```

For instance with the above configuration, an SRV record gets created for the dashboard which shows that it is on port 5000, bound to the `server` machine.
An A and a AAAA record are generated which binds `health.<lab_name>.lab` or `health.<system_name>.lab`, depending on if the system is in a lab or not, to the `server` machine.
